picks.rationale: The whole reason this case exists, and the bet with the highest ceiling: donor HA-1 TCR-T given after a second transplant aims graft-versus-leukemia at recipient blood-lineage cells while mostly sparing the tissues that drive GVHD. Bleakley's phase 1 (pmid:38683966) got 4 of 9 into CR with one remission past two years and no dose-limiting toxicity, and TSC-100/TSC-101 are recruiting on nct:NCT05473910. I won't pretend the eligibility is settled: it is double-gated on HLA-A*02:01 and a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor-negative mismatch, and none of that is genotyped yet. If the typing breaks the right way, this is the consolidation I would chase hardest.
primary_concerns: Double-gated eligibility: both HLA-A*02:01 and the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor-negative mismatch are still ungenotyped, so the whole handle may evaporate
Requires a successful HCT2 first, which is not a given in a marrow at 85% blasts with extramedullary disease
n=9 is a feasibility signal, not proof of efficacy; no efficacy powering
Depends on recipient-derived relapse confirmed by CD34-sorted STR chimerism, which is pending

picks.rationale: A refractory marrow at 85% blasts will not clear with more of the chemo that already failed; targeted CD45 radioimmunotherapy is the strongest evidence we have for dragging active disease into a transplant. SIERRA (pmid:39298738) is randomized phase 3, durable CR 22% vs 0% (p<0.0001) with EFS HR 0.23, which for this dossier is about as good as the evidence gets. The catch is that SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a FIRST allograft, so second-transplant eligibility here is unverified, and OS was flat (HR 0.99) because half the control arm crossed over. I still rank it high because this is the platform that makes every downstream cellular play, HA-1 TCR-T and DLI included, actually possible.
primary_concerns: Prior-HCT eligibility unverified; SIERRA was a first-transplant population
OS was not improved (HR 0.99), so the durable-CR benefit did not translate to survival in the trial
The entire value rests on a second transplant the patient may not tolerate
Marrow-directed RIT may not address the extramedullary thigh sarcoma

picks.rationale: A drug that physically refolds the exact mutant p53 back toward wild-type shape is the kind of mechanistic bet I will take even on thin data. In Y220C AML models (pmid:40608889) it reactivates p53 and, paired with venetoclax, restores real apoptotic killing; the solid-tumor PYNNACLE data (pmid:41740031) show ORR 20%, and 30% in KRAS-wild-type. Two things have to fall my way: TP53 confirmed aberrant (2019 mutant vs 2026 negative on a weak assay) and then confirmed as Y220C specifically, a genuine double contingency. If both land, nct:NCT06616636 (rezatapopt + azacitidine) is the myeloid slot, though the venetoclax partner the biology demands is a drug she has already progressed on.
primary_concerns: Double contingency: TP53 must be confirmed aberrant AND confirmed Y220C, both unresolved
Zero myeloid clinical data; every response so far is in solid tumors
Single-agent apoptosis is weak preclinically; it needs a venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 partner, and she is already refractory to a venetoclax-containing regimen
The myeloid trial NCT06616636 has no results posted yet

picks.rationale: CD123 is confirmed on the blasts and pivekimab is a CD123 ADC with real single-agent activity in refractory AML: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% at the recommended phase 2 dose (pmid:38423051). Preclinically it kills AML at low picomolar potency and reaches the leukemic stem-cell compartment while sparing normal progenitors (pmid:29661755), which is what you want from a cytoreduction lever ahead of transplant. It is not a cure on its own and the response rate is modest, but as a bridge that debulks without torching normal marrow it earns a slot. The veno-occlusive signal matters with a transplant planned, and benefit likely tracks quantitative CD123 density, which is still pending.
primary_concerns: ORR is modest (21%); this is a bridge, not a curative move by itself
Veno-occlusive disease signal is worrying with an HCT2 planned
Benefit is density-dependent and quantitative CD123 flow has not been done
Durability of single-agent responses in this refractory a setting is unproven

picks.rationale: Her relapse already shows clonal evolution, so betting on a single antigen invites escape; a compound CAR-T hitting both CD123 and CD33 is the hedge (nct:NCT04156256). The dual construct beat single-antigen targeting for survival across four AML xenografts (pmid:29515236), and both antigens are confirmed on her blasts. The honest problem is that this is xenograft-only with no post-allo-HCT clinical data, an unclear registry status, and CRS plus a prior-transplant history to navigate. High theoretical ceiling, almost no human evidence, which is exactly where a risktaker earns or loses the argument.
primary_concerns: No clinical efficacy data at all; the case is entirely preclinical
Trial recruitment status is listed as unknown, so it may not be an open route
CRS and on-target/off-tumor myeloablation of normal CD33/CD123 progenitors
Post-allo-HCT CAR-T eligibility and manufacturing feasibility are unaddressed

notes: Curative intent in a chemo-refractory marrow means single agents are not the game; the real question is what gets her to a second transplant and what consolidates it. I built the slate around that arc: HA-1 TCR-T is the stated priority and the biggest cure swing but is hostage to pending HLA/HA typing; Iomab-B is the enabler with the best evidence in the whole dossier; rezatapopt and the CD123/CD33 levers are cytoreduction or targeted longshots. I deliberately did not rank eprenetapopt (flagged low-yield, phase 3 miss) or gemtuzumab (on-label but only ~30% in a less-pretreated first-relapse population). No toxicity vetoes on file, so nothing here trips a hard stop, but fitness/organ-function data are missing and would change the tolerability math for Iomab-B conditioning and the ADC.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for post-transplant relapse
picks.rationale: This is the only modality on the menu with a real cure fraction and decades of GVHD and non-relapse-mortality management behind it, which is why it anchors a curative-intent plan for me. The Christopeit EBMT registry (pmid:23918951) puts 2-year OS at ~37% in the matched-related-donor subgroup that fits this patient, and her ~6-year remission after HCT1 sits on the favorable side of that curve. The catch is honest: you cannot transplant an 85%-blast marrow as-is, so HCT2 only earns rank 1 if a cytoreductive bridge brings disease burden down first. Active high-burden disease at the time of HCT2 is the single biggest thing working against her.
primary_concerns: Non-relapse mortality and GVHD in a second allograft are substantial and not fully characterized in the abstract-level registry data.
Undeliverable at 85% blasts without effective cytoreduction to a transplantable state first.
Clonal origin must be confirmed recipient-derived by CD34-sorted STR chimerism before committing, since a donor-derived leukemia would redirect the whole plan.
Organ-function and cardiac fitness are undocumented, and conditioning intensity cannot be chosen safely until they are.

picks.rationale: SIERRA is the only randomized phase 3 in this dossier (pmid:39298738), and it was built for exactly this problem: carrying active R/R AML with a high blast burden into an allograft. Durable CR was 17.1% vs 0% (p<0.0001), and the part I weight most is that grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 59.7% vs 59.2% on conventional care, so the targeted conditioning did not add toxicity on top of what these patients already face. OS was flat (HR 0.99), but that reads as a crossover artifact (52% of controls crossed to apamistamab) rather than a true efficacy failure. The main limitation is that SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so prior-HCT eligibility has to be verified against the go-forward protocol (NCT07157514) before I would bank on it.
primary_concerns: Prior allo-HCT eligibility is unverified; SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a first transplant.
Still investigational, not an approved conditioning platform.
Overall survival was not improved, and the crossover explanation, while plausible, is not proof of benefit.
The extramedullary thigh sarcoma is a sanctuary site that CD45-targeted marrow conditioning may not clear, so directed radiotherapy needs separate planning.

picks.rationale: Of everything here, this is the one agent that is FDA-approved, on-label for CD33-positive relapsed AML, and carries more than 20 years of post-marketing safety data with an AE profile I can actually predict and manage. Sievers (pmid:11432892) reported grade >=3 hyperbilirubinemia 23% and transaminase elevation 17% with a well-worn VOD monitoring algorithm, which matters because a second transplant is on the table and hepatic/VOD risk stacks peri-transplant. I am honest that single-agent depth in first relapse was only ~30%, and this patient is further along with FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure and extramedullary disease, so I position this as a CD33-directed cytoreductive bridge, not a definitive answer. Quantitative CD33 antigen density is still pending and should anchor the go/no-go.
primary_concerns: Modest single-agent remission depth (~30%) in a less heavily pretreated population than this patient.
Veno-occlusive disease risk compounds a planned HCT2; needs an adequate interval and hepatic monitoring, and argues for fractionated dosing.
Benefit prediction depends on the pending quantitative CD33 antigen-density readout, not the qualitative flow positivity on file.

picks.intervention_label: FLAMSA-RIC sequential chemotherapy + reduced-intensity allo-HCT + prophylactic DLI
picks.rationale: If HCT2 is the goal, FLAMSA-RIC is the best-characterized way to actually deliver it in refractory disease: sequential cytoreduction straight into a reduced-intensity allograft, with prophylactic DLI from day +120. Schmid's prospective cohort (pmid:16110027) reported 88% CR and 2-year OS 42%, with the refractory and adverse-cytogenetics subgroup doing as well as lower-risk patients, and 31 of 75 used HLA-identical sibling donors, the same donor situation here. GVHD, including DLI-associated GVHD, is the principal risk and is well mapped in this setting. It overlaps with rank 1 by design, so I list it as the concrete sequencing rather than a competing modality.
primary_concerns: GVHD from reduced-intensity conditioning plus prophylactic DLI is the dominant risk and per-term toxicity is not tabulated in the source abstract.
Overlaps with the HCT2 platform in rank 1 rather than adding an independent option.
An older regimen whose conditioning intensity depends on cardiac and organ-function fitness that has not been assessed.

notes: The case was submitted for the HLA-restricted immunotherapy axis (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME), and I deliberately ranked none of it. Three reasons, in order. First, eligibility is doubly unresolved: HLA-A*02:01 typing is a chart placeholder, and HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of both patient and sibling donor has not been done, so candidacy cannot even be established. Second, the closest precedent (Bleakley HA-1 TCR-T, pmid:38683966, n=9, 4/9 CR, 0 DLTs) reports no per-term grade-level AE table; the Blood 2024 full-text safety breakdown could not be retrieved. I will not place a phase-1 cell product with an unretrievable toxicity table above an approved agent or an established transplant platform in a patient whose organ function is not characterized. Third, all of it is post-HCT2 consolidation by design, not a current-state answer for 85% blasts. If typing resolves favorably and disease is cytoreduced, TSC-100/101 (NCT05473910) becomes a reasonable consolidation conversation, but it earns that slot after the transplant, not instead of it. The same logic parks rezatapopt: doubly contingent (confirm the TP53 aberration, then confirm Y220C), solid-tumor-only clinical data (pmid:41740031), and myeloid data predicting it needs a venetoclax partner rather than single-agent use (pmid:40608889). CD123 agents (tagraxofusp, pivekimab) are on-mechanism but bring capillary-leak and VOD signals into a fitness-unassessed, pre-transplant patient, so they sit behind the approved CD33 handle for me until organ-function data land.

picks.rationale: SIERRA is the only randomized phase 3 in this dossier, and it hit its registered primary endpoint: durable CR at 180-plus days 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001, EFS HR 0.23. Two things keep me off full confidence. OS was flat (HR 0.99, p=0.96), which the authors pin on 52% crossover, and dCR is a durable-remission surrogate rather than an OS win. It is also open-label, so RoB2 lands at 'some concerns' for outcome ascertainment, and every enrolled patient was going into a first transplant, so the HCT2 eligibility read is not settled.
primary_concerns: RoB2 domain 4/5: open-label, dCR ascertained without blinding
Registered primary endpoint is dCR (surrogate); ITT OS null (HR 0.99, p=0.96) with 52% crossover confounding the survival read
Eligibility mismatch: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients; the prior-allo-HCT / HCT2 setting is unverified against the protocol

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for relapse after first allo-HCT
picks.rationale: The realistic backbone, and the honest number is 37% two-year OS in the matched-related-donor subgroup of a 179-patient EBMT registry. That is retrospective and ROBINS-I Serious on confounding and selection, and 37% is a subgroup rather than the whole-cohort 25%. His roughly six-year first remission pushes the odds his way; the 85% marrow blasts going into HCT2 pull hard the other way.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I Serious: retrospective registry, confounding by patient/disease selection into a second transplant
37% is the related-donor subgroup, not the pooled 25% cohort estimate
Active high-burden disease at transplant is the dominant adverse survival driver in the same analysis

picks.intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) for AML relapse after allo-HCT
picks.rationale: The one comparative signal in the transplant set, 21% vs 9% two-year OS at P=0.04 after adjustment, but that is confounding by indication wearing a p-value. The benefit sat in the remission or favorable-karyotype group (~56%); patients given DLI in aplasia or with active disease came in around 15%, and with 85% blasts and adverse cytogenetics he is squarely in that worse stratum. I read it as an argument for cytoreduction before any DLI, not for DLI on its own.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I Serious: confounding by indication; DLI recipients selected on fitness and disease control
Adjusted benefit is subgroup-driven; the active-disease stratum this patient falls in shows ~15% 2-yr OS
Non-randomized no-DLI comparator

picks.rationale: On-label and on-mechanism for his confirmed CD33+ blasts, and the largest single-arm dataset among the antigen-directed options at 142 patients, roughly 30% remission. But that 30% is CR+CRp with no OS attached, in first-relapse patients without an antecedent hematologic disorder, and he is well past that population: prior MDS, FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure, extramedullary sarcoma. Quantitative CD33 density is still pending, and the hepatic/VOD signal is not trivial with an HCT2 planned.
primary_concerns: Single-arm, surrogate endpoint (CR+CRp), no OS/PFS; ROBINS-I Serious
Registration population less pretreated (first relapse, no antecedent MDS) than this patient; external-validity gap
ADC benefit tracks CD33 antigen density, which is not yet quantified

picks.rationale: This is the handle the case was built around, so let me be plain: it also carries the thinnest evidence in the dossier. Bleakley's Blood 2024 report is a single-arm phase 1, n=9, 4/9 CR, no DLTs. That is feasibility, not efficacy, and ROBINS-I Serious. Eligibility is doubly gated on values that are all still pending: HLA-A*02:01, plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor-negative mismatch that needs genotyping in both the patient and the sibling. The low rank is about evidence maturity and unresolved eligibility, not a verdict on the biology.
primary_concerns: n=9 single-arm phase 1; endpoint is feasibility/safety, not powered for efficacy; ROBINS-I Serious
Efficacy read rests on 4/9 CR with no comparator, and the per-term AE table could not be retrieved from the full text
Double eligibility gate unresolved: HLA-A*02:01 and recipient/donor HA-1 genotype both pending, plus recipient-origin relapse not yet proven by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism

notes: Two things I deliberately kept off the ranking on evidence grounds. Rezatapopt has genuine Y220C proof-of-concept but only in solid tumors (PYNNACLE, ORR 20%, all responders KRAS wild-type), the myeloid trial NCT06616636 has posted nothing, and here it is doubly contingent: confirm a TP53 aberration at all, then confirm it is Y220C, off a 2019-mutant-versus-2026-negative discrepancy read on a 2%-LOD/no-CNV panel. Eprenetapopt is worse for our purposes; its phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its CR primary endpoint and myeloid development has largely stopped, so a 64% frontline ORR from an n=39 phase 1 subgroup is not something I would lean on, and it is a line mismatch besides. Whole ranking sits downstream of the confirmatory workup: HLA typing, TP53/Y220C resolution, quantitative CD33/CD123 density, and STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts to establish recipient-origin relapse before any mHAg-directed cell therapy is on the table. Note on RoB provenance: for several rows (Iomab-B, gemtuzumab, pivekimab, HA-1 TCR-T) only abstract-level data or partial full text was retrievable, so per-grade AE tables and some domain-level RoB judgments are read off abstracts, not the primary full text.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
picks.rationale: ELN 2022 (Dohner, Blood 2022;140:1345) puts a second allo-HCT at the center of curative-intent management for AML that relapses after transplant, on the condition that the marrow is first brought back into remission. Her edge is the ~6-year first remission: in the EBMT related-donor subgroup that maps to roughly 37% 2-year OS after HCT2 (Christopeit 2013), better than the cohort overall. NCCN AML v4.2026 keeps second transplant among the category 2A options for post-transplant relapse in fit patients, and ECOG 1 with no vetoed modality keeps her inside that population. It is the platform the rest of the plan, including any HLA-restricted consolidation, has to be built on.
primary_concerns: 85% marrow blasts plus a thigh myeloid sarcoma mean HCT2 cannot be delivered up front; the guideline recommendation is explicitly conditioned on cytoreduction first, which is the unsolved step here.
No cardiac or organ-function labs are on file, so the fitness assumptions ELN/NCCN attach to a second transplant are unverified.
TP53-aberrant complex-karyotype disease escaped graft-versus-leukemia once already; a durable HCT2 is far from assured even with a good first remission.

picks.rationale: Both NCCN AML v4.2026 and ELN 2022 name clinical-trial enrollment as the preferred route in relapsed/refractory AML, and this handle is the stated reason for the run: HA-1-directed donor TCR-T (TSC-100, NCT05473910; Fred Hutch platform, pmid 38683966). The phase 1 signal is early but real, with 4 of 9 recurrent post-HCT patients reaching or holding CR and no dose-limiting toxicity. It slots onto an HCT2 as consolidation, which is where the guideline-endorsed adoptive-cell approach for post-transplant relapse actually lives. I rank it second rather than first because eligibility is undetermined, not established.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is gated on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, and neither the patient nor the sibling donor has been genotyped; she sits in an undetermined enrolling population, not a confirmed-eligible one.
The guideline support is for 'enroll in a trial,' not for TCR-T as such; this is a phase-1 investigational product with no consensus category behind it.
It is post-transplant consolidation, so it does nothing for the 85%-blast marrow that has to be controlled first.

picks.rationale: Gemtuzumab is the one on-label, guideline-listed drug in play: NCCN AML v4.2026 carries single-agent gemtuzumab (category 2A) for CD33-positive relapsed AML, and her blasts are CD33+ by flow. I read it as a cytoreductive bridge toward HCT2, not as definitive therapy. The honest ceiling is modest, about 30% overall remission in first relapse (Sievers 2001, pmid 11432892), and she is well past first relapse with extramedullary disease. Quantitative CD33 density is still pending, and that is the readout that tells us whether ADC-level expression is even there.
primary_concerns: The single-agent remission figure comes from a first-relapse population less pretreated than this patient; carrying it over to post-FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure with a myeloid sarcoma overstates likely benefit.
Calicheamicin hepatotoxicity and VOD are the class risk and matter directly with an HCT2 planned soon after (Sievers reported grade 3+ hyperbilirubinemia in 23%).
Qualitative CD33 positivity is not antigen density; committing before the quantitative flow is target selection done backwards.

picks.intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) for AML relapse after allo-HCT
picks.rationale: Sibling DLI sits squarely inside ELN 2022's framing of post-transplant relapse: immunosuppression taper plus cytoreduction plus adoptive cellular therapy is the combination they credit with occasional durable remissions. Her late relapse (>5 months, here ~6 years) is exactly the feature that predicts DLI benefit in the EBMT series (Schmid 2007, pmid 17909197; 21% vs 9% 2-year OS with vs without DLI). The catch is burden: given in active high-burden disease, that same series shows ~15% 2-year OS, so DLI has to follow cytoreduction, not lead it. I treat it as an adjunct to the transplant platform, not a standalone.
primary_concerns: At 85% blasts she is in the active-disease/high-burden DLI group where the registry outcome is worst; DLI alone is not defensible here.
GVHD is the characteristic toxicity and would complicate a subsequent HCT2.
The registry benefit is a minority effect and selection-confounded; it calibrates expectations rather than promising much.

picks.rationale: SIERRA is the strongest evidence in this dossier for getting an active, high-blast marrow into an allo-HCT: a randomized phase 3 with durable CR 22% vs 0% and EFS HR 0.23 (Gyurkocza 2025, pmid 39298738). That maps almost exactly onto her problem, an 85%-blast marrow and an extramedullary site standing between her and HCT2. Where I hold back is guideline status: CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning is still investigational and not adopted by NCCN or ELN as a standard, and SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a first transplant, so the prior-HCT fit has to be checked against the go-forward protocol (NCT07157514). Strong platform signal, off the enrolled population, and pre-guideline.
primary_concerns: SIERRA's pivotal population was heading to a first allo-HCT; using it to condition an HCT2 extrapolates beyond the enrolled group.
Phase 3 evidence exists, but NCCN/ELN have not taken up CD45 RIT conditioning as standard, so this is a trial-route pick, not a consensus one.
OS was flat in SIERRA (HR 0.99) once control patients crossed over, so the durable-CR advantage may not convert into a survival gain.

notes: Two handles I left off the ranked list on guideline-fit grounds. Rezatapopt is doubly contingent (TP53 has to be confirmed, then shown to be Y220C), and even then the only myeloid data are a phase-1b with no results posted (NCT06616636); the pivotal PYNNACLE program is solid-tumor only. Eprenetapopt is worse for consensus: pan-reactivator, phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint, myeloid development largely halted. Neither belongs in a guideline-anchored ranking yet. The whole plan hinges on pending workup: resolve TP53 (2019 report + p53 IHC + 17p FISH), pull HLA-A*02:01 and HA-1/HA-2 genotypes on patient and sibling, and confirm recipient-origin relapse by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism before any cellular option moves from 'undetermined' to eligible.

picks.intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after second allo-HCT (Bleakley platform; TSC-100/TSC-101, ALLOHA)
picks.rationale: This is the handle the case was submitted for, and it fits what the patient asked for: curative intent, a trial they will travel for, and a graft-versus-leukemia mechanism that spares the tissues driving GVHD. Bleakley's phase 1 got 4 of 9 recurrent post-HCT patients into CR with no dose-limiting toxicity, and TSC-100/101 (ALLOHA, NCT05473910) runs the same mechanism on the back of a fresh matched transplant. The honest catch is eligibility: it needs HLA-A*02:01, a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor-negative mismatch genotyped in both the patient and the sibling, and recipient-origin relapse confirmed by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism, none of which is resolved yet. I still rank it first, because retrieving the 2020 typing and genotyping the pair is fast and cheap and is the only thing standing between the patient and the option they came here for.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: curative intent, prefers_trials incl. travel, no toxicity veto tripped, efficacy-leaning
In tension: eligibility unresolved until HLA-A*02:01 typing is retrieved and HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient AND sibling donor is done
Sequencing: delivered on the back of HCT2 (rank 2) and requires recipient-origin relapse confirmed by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism

picks.intervention_label: Targeted radioimmunotherapy conditioning (Iomab-B / 131I-apamistamab) into second allo-HCT; FLAMSA-RIC as the sequencing alternative
picks.rationale: A second transplant is the platform the HA-1/HA-2 cells are delivered on, so honoring the primary preference means getting the patient safely to HCT2 with an 85%-blast marrow. SIERRA (phase 3, pmid:39298738) is the strongest evidence that CD45-targeted radioimmunotherapy can carry active R/R AML into an allograft, with durable CR 17% versus 0%, and FLAMSA-RIC (pmid:16110027) reaches the same endpoint by sequencing. The roughly 6-year remission after the first transplant puts this patient in the more favorable band of the HCT2 registry (about 37% 2-year OS in the related-donor subgroup, pmid:23918951). Curative intent, a modality the patient explicitly kept on the table, and no veto in play; the open axis is fitness, which is undocumented and should set conditioning intensity.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: curative intent, no modality ruled out (HCT2 explicitly acceptable), no veto, efficacy lean
In tension: SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a FIRST transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility for the go-forward apamistamab study (NCT07157514) must be verified
Open axis flagged by the patient's own file: no ECOG/cardiac/organ-function data yet; the 0.75 efficacy weight should be revisited once fitness is known

picks.intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (CD123 ADC) as cytoreductive bridge to HCT2 / cellular consolidation
picks.rationale: To reach HCT2 and a cellular consolidation you first have to bring an 85%-blast marrow down, and re-running the FLAG-IDA scaffold the disease already failed is not the way to do it. Pivekimab is a CD123 ADC with single-agent activity in R/R AML (ORR 21%, pmid:38423051) against the patient's confirmed CD123-positive blasts, without stacking onto a backbone that has already lost. It clears the preference filter, no veto and trial-acceptable, with two honest caveats: quantitative CD123 antigen density is still pending and would sharpen the choice, and the veno-occlusive signal matters with a transplant ahead. Tagraxofusp is a reasonable alternative but carries capillary-leak risk that argues for fitness data before committing.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: efficacy-leaning bridge, no veto, trial route available
In tension: quantitative CD123 density (requested) not yet back; VOD signal is relevant with HCT2 planned
Role is cytoreduction, not curative on its own; it earns its rank only as a bridge to ranks 1-2

picks.intervention_label: WT1 HLA-A*02:01 TCR-T (WT1-TCRc4 / FH-WT1-E50); A*24:02 WT1-siTCR as the fallback lever
picks.rationale: If the HA-1/HA-2 pair does not mismatch but the patient is A*02:01-positive, WT1 keeps the HLA-restricted axis alive instead of foreclosing it. The Chapuis WT1-TCRc4 work (pmid:31235963) held 12 high-risk AML patients relapse-free post-transplant, and FH-WT1-E50 (NCT07645469) carries the current version, best positioned as post-cytoreduction or post-HCT2 consolidation rather than for florid relapse. If A*02:01 comes back negative, A*24:02 opens the WT1-siTCR lever (pmid:28860210), which is why both alleles should be typed in parallel before anyone forecloses this pathway. Same preference fit as rank 1, with weaker evidence and a disease-state mismatch at the current blast burden.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: same HLA-restricted, curative-intent, trial-acceptable profile the run was built around
In tension: prophylaxis/MRD evidence base, not active-relapse salvage; gated on A*02:01 (or A*24:02) still pending
Kept explicitly so an A*02:01-positive but HA-non-mismatched result does not close the immunotherapy axis the patient prioritized

picks.intervention_label: Dual CD33/CD123 compound CAR-T (antigen-escape hedge); on-label gemtuzumab as the available CD33 alternative
picks.rationale: Given the clonal evolution documented between 2019 and 2026, single-antigen cytoreduction invites escape, and the patient carries both CD33 and CD123. A compound CD33/CD123 CAR-T (NCT04156256) covers both antigens and is the escape hedge the profile flags, trial-acceptable and consistent with the curative goal. The honesty here is real: it is early-phase with xenograft-only support, no post-allo-HCT data, and CRS plus prior-transplant eligibility are open questions. On-label gemtuzumab (pmid:11432892) is the lower-ceiling but immediately available CD33 option if a trial slot does not materialize.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: no veto, trial-acceptable, curative-intent framing
In tension: earliest-phase evidence of any pick; xenograft-only, no post-HCT data, CRS and prior-transplant eligibility unresolved
Quantitative CD33/CD123 density (requested) would gate the ADC/CAR decision it depends on

notes: Deliberately did NOT foreground TP53/rezatapopt: it is doubly contingent (confirm the aberration, then confirm it is Y220C) and sits off the HLA-restricted axis that is the stated reason for this run; worth resolving in parallel but not a preference-carrying pick today. Not a yes-machine on the 0.75 efficacy weight either: the patient's own file flags that no ECOG/cardiac/organ-function data exist yet, so the efficacy lean and the conditioning intensity for ranks 2-3 should be revisited once fitness is assessed. The single load-bearing next action that unlocks rank 1 is not a drug: retrieve the 2020 high-resolution HLA-A typing, genotype HA-1/HA-2 in the patient and the sibling donor, and run STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts to confirm recipient-origin relapse.
